ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: Generally considered the first known kingdom of Southeast Asia, Funan traded through its port of Óc Eo, where Roman gold medallions and Indian and Persian goods were found.
A confederation of Cham principalities on the coast of present-day Vietnam, whose fleets controlled the spice and silk trade of the South China Sea from the 7th to the 10th century.
The Khmer principalities that broke from Funan absorbed it under Isanavarman I, before Jayavarman II proclaimed the Khmer Empire in 802.
From Palembang in Sumatra this sea power ruled the Strait of Malacca, taxed China-India shipping and became a renowned centre of Buddhist learning.
One of the largest Buddhist monuments in the world, the temple was built in central Java under the Sailendra dynasty, closely connected to Srivijaya.
Founded in 802, the empire ruled much of mainland Southeast Asia from Angkor, where vast reservoirs and canals paid for Angkor Wat and Angkor Thom.
The first state to unite the Irrawaddy valley built some 10,000 Buddhist monuments on the plain of Bagan before Mongol invasions in the 1280s broke it apart.
The high point of Hindu-Buddhist Java claimed suzerainty over much of the archipelago, its fleets paid for by Brantas rice and the spice trade.
The Siamese kingdom on the Chao Phraya absorbed Sukhothai in 1438 and welcomed Chinese, Japanese, Persian and European merchants until Burma destroyed it in 1767.
Founded about 1400 by Parameswara under Ming protection, the port became the great entrepôt of the strait and a centre of Islamic learning until the Portuguese took it in 1511.
